lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I've reviewed the official guidance. Now let me ask you some questions to determine your eligibility.

First question: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names (or just first names) and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have Alex, who is 3 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Next question: **Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Are you paying at least the same amount as the Child Benefit rate (or providing the equivalent in kind) towards looking after Alex?** This could include things like food, clothes, or pocket money.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards Alex's upkeep. I help out with things like clothes and essentials.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To better understand your situation, I need to ask:

**What is the approximate amount you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month?** (The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, so around £110 per month)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information - £50 per week is above the Child Benefit rate for one child.

Now I need to ask: **Who does Alex currently live with?** (For example, the other parent, a relative, or someone else?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with their other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

One more important question: **Is the other parent currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or do you know if anyone else is claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the other parent isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and no one else is claiming it either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you a UK resident with the right to reside in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to reside?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a UK resident with the right to reside here.

Thank you for answering all my questions. Let me now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit based on the information you've provided.

Based on what you've told me:
- You have a child, Alex, who is 3 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
- Alex doesn't live with you but lives with their other parent
- You contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for one child)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the official guidance, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You're usually considered responsible for a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money.

Since you're contributing £50 per week (which exceeds the Child Benefit rate) and no one else is claiming for Alex, you meet the eligibility criteria.
